questions.question: How does tool execution work end to end in the TypeScript SDK?
questions.reference_answer: composio.tools.execute(slug, body) validates the params with ToolExecuteParamsSchema, fetches the tool schema with getRawComposioToolBySlug (using the explicit version or the SDK's toolkitVersions), then calls executeWithTool. executeWithTool runs applyBeforeExecuteModifiers (file-upload staging when dangerouslyAllowAutoUploadDownloadFiles is on, then the caller's beforeExecute), then executeComposioTool, which resolves the toolkit version (throwing ComposioToolVersionRequiredError if it is 'latest' and dangerouslySkipVersionCheck is not set) and POSTs to client.tools.execute through a client with retries disabled, mapping API errors via handleToolExecutionError. Finally applyAfterExecuteModifiers downloads any s3url files (when auto-download is on) and runs afterExecute. Provider-wrapped tools reach the same executeWithTool/execute path through createExecuteToolFn / createExecuteFnForProviders with dangerouslySkipVersionCheck defaulting to true.

questions.question: How do custom tools work?
questions.reference_answer: In the TypeScript SDK a custom tool is created with createCustomTool(slug, {name, description, inputParams: z.object(...), execute, extendsToolkit?, preload?}) in ts/packages/core/src/models/CustomTool.ts; it validates the slug and options, converts the Zod input schema to JSON Schema and returns a CustomTool handle. Custom tools (and custom toolkits from createCustomToolkit) are session-scoped: they are passed via experimental.customTools / customToolkits when creating or using a Tool Router session, serialized inline to the backend, and mapped to final slugs with a LOCAL_ prefix (LOCAL_<SLUG> or LOCAL_<TOOLKIT>_<SLUG>). When a session executes a slug that matches a custom tool (findCustomTool by final or unique original slug), executeCustomTool runs it in-process: it validates arguments with the original Zod schema, calls the tool's execute(input, sessionContext), and returns {data, error: null, successful: true} or {successful: false, error} on validation failure or thrown errors. Non-custom slugs go to the backend.

questions.question: How do the Python and TypeScript SDKs differ?
questions.reference_answer: They mirror the same model surface (tools, toolkits, triggers, auth configs, connected accounts, MCP, sessions/tool router, both defaulting to an OpenAI provider and enforcing the 'latest' toolkit-version check on manual execution) but differ in idiom and some behavior. TypeScript (ts/packages/core) is async/Promise-based, uses camelCase options (userId, toolkitVersions, dangerouslySkipVersionCheck), validates with Zod, passes modifiers as option objects (beforeExecute/afterExecute/modifySchema), instruments async methods via telemetry.instrument, and can read the API key from the CLI's user-data file. Python (python/composio) is synchronous, uses snake_case kwargs (user_id, toolkit_versions, dangerously_skip_version_check), expresses modifiers with decorators (before_execute, after_execute, schema_modifier) in _modifiers.py, traces calls with a trace_method wrapper gated by an allow_tracking context var, raises ApiKeyNotProvidedError at construction when no key is found, and creates a fresh provider per SDK instance. The CLI exists only in TypeScript (ts/packages/cli). Provider integrations are split into separate packages in both (ts/packages/providers/*, python/providers/*).
key_facts: TS is async/Promise-based with camelCase params; Python is synchronous with snake_case kwargs
Python modifiers are decorators (before_execute/after_execute/schema_modifier); TS passes modifier functions in an options object
both default to an OpenAI provider and both refuse 'latest' toolkit versions on manual execution unless skipped
the CLI is TypeScript-only
forbidden_claims: the Python SDK is a thin wrapper that calls the TypeScript SDK

questions.question: How do triggers work and how do I subscribe to trigger events?

questions.question: What is the difference between agentic and non-agentic providers?
questions.reference_answer: Both extend BaseProvider (ts/packages/core/src/provider/BaseProvider.ts). A non-agentic provider (BaseNonAgenticProvider, _isAgentic = false) only converts tools into the LLM's tool-schema format: wrapTool(tool) / wrapTools(tools) take no execute function, and the application runs tool calls itself (e.g. provider.executeToolCall / handleToolCalls, which call executeTool/executeToolForTarget). OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Cloudflare are non-agentic. An agentic provider (BaseAgenticProvider, _isAgentic = true) gets an execute function: wrapTool(tool, executeTool) / wrapTools(tools, executeTool) produce framework tools (e.g. LangChain) that execute themselves when the agent framework calls them. In Python the equivalents are NonAgenticProvider.wrap_tool(tool) and AgenticProvider.wrap_tool(tool, execute_tool) (python/composio/core/provider).

agentic providers' wrapTool/wrapTools receive an executeTool function so the framework executes tools itself

questions.question: How are webhook signatures verified?
questions.reference_answer: composio.triggers.verifyWebhook({payload, signature, secret, id, timestamp, tolerance}) in ts/packages/core/src/models/Triggers.ts validates the params (naming the missing webhook-id / webhook-timestamp / webhook-signature headers), checks the timestamp is within tolerance seconds (default 300) when tolerance > 0, then verifyWebhookSignature: it requires non-empty payload, signature, secret, id and timestamp, extracts the 'v1,<base64>' entries from the space-separated webhook-signature header, computes HMAC-SHA256 over `${webhookId}.${webhookTimestamp}.${payload}` with the secret (hmacSha256Base64 in utils/crypto.ts), and compares with timingSafeEqual; mismatch throws ComposioWebhookSignatureVerificationError. questions.question: How is telemetry collected and can it be disabled?
questions.reference_answer: In TypeScript, the Composio constructor calls telemetry.setup(...) only when allowTracking is true (default true via CONFIG_DEFAULTS), and instruments the Composio instance, the provider, and model classes (e.g. Tools) with telemetry.instrument, which wraps async methods to record the method name, duration and errors. questions.question: How are errors from tool execution handled and surfaced to the user?
questions.reference_answer: Validation problems throw typed errors before any call (ValidationError for bad params, ComposioToolVersionRequiredError for an unpinned 'latest' version, ComposioToolNotFoundError / ComposioToolFetchError when fetching the tool fails). If the execute API call itself throws, executeComposioTool passes the error to handleToolExecutionError (ts/packages/core/src/errors/ToolErrors.ts), which maps API error code 1803 to ComposioConnectedAccountNotFoundError and wraps everything else in ComposioToolExecutionError('Error executing the tool <slug>') with the original error as cause; cancellation is rethrown as ComposioRequestCancelledError. Failures reported by the tool itself are not thrown: the response comes back as {data, error, successful: false}. Custom tools likewise return successful: false with the validation or thrown error message. Providers pass results back to the LLM (e.g. AnthropicProvider returns {error} JSON when result.error is set).
